title: Annotatio III §.IV: Melanchthon to the Elector — silence quarrelers; keep one Forma of Paul’s κοινωνία words; declare the Supper’s fruit; the Son is present for man, not for bread
pass_a_gloss: It helps to remember certain words: I approve (Melanchthon writes to the Elector) the Counsel of the Most Illustrious Elector, that he commanded silence to those quarreling on both sides, lest distraction arise in the tender Church and the weak be troubled in that place and neighborhood, and I would wish the quarrelers on either side to be away. Secondly, the contentious having been removed, it is profitable that the rest agree on one Form of words, and in this controversy it is best to retain the words of Paul: The bread which we break is the κοινωνία of the body, and one must speak copiously of the fruit of the Supper, that men may be stirred to love of this pledge and frequent use; and the word κοινωνία must be declared. And with a few things inserted: The Son of God is present, says Melanchthon, in the Ministry of the Gospel and there he is certainly efficacious in believers, and he is present not on account of the Bread but on account of Man, as he says: Abide in me, and I in you. Likewise: I am in my Father, and you in me and I in you. And by these true Consolations he makes us members to himself and testifies that he will vivify our bodies.
pass_b_english: Some of Melanchthon’s words to the Elector are worth keeping: he approves the Elector’s counsel that both sides’ quarrelers be silenced, lest the tender church split and the weak nearby be troubled — and he wishes such quarrelers gone from either party.

Second, once the contentious are removed, the rest should agree on one Forma of words; best here is to keep Paul’s: the bread we break is the κοινωνία of the body — and to speak richly of the Supper’s fruit so people love this pledge and use it often, declaring what κοινωνία means.

Melanchthon inserts: the Son of God is present in the ministry of the Gospel and efficacious in believers — present not for the bread but for the man ("Abide in me…"; "I am in my Father, and you in me…"). By these consolations he makes us his members and promises to vivify our bodies.
source_text: Verba quaedam memorari juvat: Probo (scribit Melanchthon ad Electorem) Consilium Illustrissimi Electoris, quod rixantibus utrinque mandavit silentium, ne distractio fiat in tenera Ecclesia & infirmi turbentur in illo loco & vicinia, & optarem rixatores in utraque parte abesse. Secundò, remotis contentiosis, prodest reliquos de una Forma verborum convenire & in hac controversia optimum est retinere verba Pauli: Panis quem frangimus κοινωνία ἐστὶ τοῦ σώματος, & copiosè de fructu caenae dicendum est, ut incitentur Homines ad amorem hujus pignoris & crebrum usum; & vocabulum κοινωνία declarandum est. Paucisque interfertis: Adest, inquit Melanchthon, Filius Dei in Ministerio Evangelii & ibi certè efficax est in credentibus, ac adest, non propter Panem, sed propter Hominem, sicut inquit: Manete in me, & ego in vobis. Item: Ego sum in Patre meo, & vos in me & Ego in vobis. Et his veris Consolationibus facit nos sibi membra & testatur se corpora nostra vivificaturum esse.
